The model wrapper

In one line: each call of the API to a language model goes through one module, which asks DeepSeek first, asks Gemini when DeepSeek fails, and records the tokens of each attempt.

What it is

  • A model is a language model of a vendor. The API sends it a system prompt and the messages of the chat, and it answers with text.
  • A role is the job of a call: the router, the extractor, the observer, the composer or the Advisor (PD7a).
  • The fallback is the second model. The API asks it when the first model gives no valid answer.
  • Tokens are the units that a vendor counts and bills. Cached tokens are the start of a prompt that the vendor saw before. They cost much less.

How it fits our project

a role (T-12, T-13, …) ──▶ models.json() or models.text() ──▶ DeepSeek (deepseek-flash)
                                     │                         │ timeout, 5xx or 429
                                     │                         ▼
                                     │                  Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash-lite)
                                     └──▶ the event model_called, and one log line for each attempt
  • One module: apps/api/src/models/. No other code calls a model (PD7, ADR-0014). It sends the chat request of the OpenAI format with fetch, because both vendors accept it.
  • Two kinds of call: models.json({ req, role, system, messages, schema, session }) asks in the JSON mode of the vendor and parses the answer with the Zod schema. models.text({ … }) gives text, for the composer and the Advisor.
  • The fallback: a timeout, a 5xx or a 429 goes to Gemini. An answer that fails the schema goes to DeepSeek one more time, then to Gemini. When Gemini also fails, the module reports the error and throws ModelUnavailable. The role then selects what the user sees.
  • The record: each attempt writes the analytics event model_called with the role, the model, the tokens in, the cached tokens, the tokens out, the time, the fallback, the outcome and the session. The sum of the tokens of one session gives the cost of one interview (PD5). The event has no text.
  • The settings: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY. Without both, the API calls no model. MODEL_PRIMARY, MODEL_FALLBACK and MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS have defaults. A model name that starts with gemini goes to Gemini, and the others go to DeepSeek.
  • The live check: a moderator sends POST /v1/admin/model-check. The API asks each model one short question, with no fallback, and shows which model answered, the tokens and the time.

The choice we made

  • DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for all roles, and the Gemini Flash-Lite tier as the fallback: PD7.
  • A record in the analytics database, and a check route for moderators: #185.

Gotchas

  • Put the fixed system prompt in system, and the changing text in messages. The cache of each vendor works only on a start of the prompt that does not change.
  • In the JSON mode, the prompt must contain the word "json" and show the shape of the answer. If not, a vendor can refuse the call.
  • A 4xx other than 429, for example a bad key, throws at once, with no fallback. The check route shows a bad key after each deploy.
  • DeepSeek costs more from 06:30 to 09:30 and from 11:30 to 15:30 IST, from Monday to Friday (model selection).
  • In the tests, stub the global fetch. The tests of apps/api/test/models.test.ts show how.
